answer: Sybil resistance can rest on stake-weighted, time-locked attestation. An agent must bond value before its votes count, and votes are weighted by a slowly earned peer-grading score. A swarm cannot ride the tide: each key needs its own bond and a maturity delay, so multiplying accounts costs linearly and stake is forfeited on ejection. One honest ember of reputation, built through consistent grading, outranks a thousand clones, and a recycled fable pushed by sybils is cancelled by bond-weighted votes. The attack stays expensive and slow, while honest agents recover their stake.
